overall: Tomorrow (Sunday, July 5) in Atlanta is expected to be mostly sunny with another hot and humid day, featuring a chance of afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms developing after 2pm. The NWS forecasts a high near 94°F with heat index values reaching up to 100°F, continuing the oppressive heat pattern seen today. Afternoon storm activity (30% PoP) could provide some cloud cover or a brief cooling effect but is unlikely to significantly suppress the daytime high.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is substantial and is a key uncertainty flag: ECMWF and HRRR are running hot at approximately 98.0°F and 96.0°F respectively, while GFS and WEATHER_COM are considerably cooler at 87.9°F and 85.5°F — a spread of over 12°F between extremes. NBM (~92.2°F) and GEM (~90.5°F) cluster closer to the ensemble mean of 93.0°F, which also aligns well with the NWS narrative forecast of ~94°F, lending moderate credibility to the mid-range solution.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model expects a TMAX of 93.0°F, in close agreement with the NWS point forecast of ~94°F and the prior-day observed high of 91.4°F suggesting modest day-over-day warming. The active Kalshi odd-bucket market top bucket (93-94F at 21.1%) aligns directly with these central estimates, but the Tier 4 signal rating (expected accuracy ~32%), high inter-model spread, and afternoon convective risk all indicate low confidence — caution is warranted. A best estimate of 93.0°F is reasonable, but the wide model disagreement means outcomes anywhere from the upper 80s to upper 90s cannot be ruled out.
